Always here to provide the most unassuming and unexciting answer, which is I don't think the white cat currently has a significant meaning until its direct participation in the future events proves me wrong.

Adding a cat in the scene is a conscious choice yes; but all events function without it, and there are more than one scenario where inserting supernatural meaning due to its presence is outright unnecessary. I could extend my pass even to Dyed Orange, Drenched in Sun under some unprovable hypotheses like "something has been watching Sensei via the white cat", but that to me didn't work well with Forty Degrees Below Zero where Karin scooped the cat and ran off happily if you lied to her. Events like these that are very slice-of-life-ish hold me back and have me thinking, "yea that's probably just a cat".

edit2: similar feeling goes to Io's mummified cat and a slew of "cat props" in The Light of the Last Summer. If I can't explain the meaning behind or the potential causality in between, it'd be regarded as nonsignificant.

1. At first I was quite bewildered by Sana's experience; hers didn't fall quite well onto the linear regression I drew based off Noriko's and Futaba's experiences, letting me to questioning whether or not all TSS would be under the same tightly written principle or objective in terms of content, or they would instead be merely under broad strokes like "girls getting teleported somewhere while remaining conscious".

Then I realized that Sana probably never really attended her TSS, did she? She got teleported to a plane "four days early" and her tour mentioned "a tour of a school", then she got "sent back" to Kumon-mi early before any of that happened because apparently she "broke the rules???" Did she get kicked out by Sekaori or did she get rescued by John? (there is like 2% logic in that last sentence and it's making me uncomfortable)

2. Seeing Shota was a pleasant surprise, and a nice throwback to what Yasu told Sana about feeling his presence on the beach during beach wars.

Shota's presence and...maybe John as well (?) implied that this particular plain could be the plain a soul goes when they die, though I suppose he could also be recruited to this plain specifically for TSS purpose.

3. The most surprising thing is not seeing young Akira, but seeing Sekaori in that particular form. From the looks of it, she wasn't an innocent trespasser to this plain like Sana or young Akira, or a trapped soul like Shota, but a lot more like another agent equivalent to Mr. Pegasus. Most importantly, it's the question "Is it the idea of God you despise? Or have simply not found the right one?" that insinuated the fact despite not believing in gods, Sekai had found the right one for her either before or after she died, and she was operating under some god-given principles.

But one thing I couldn't get my head around is again, her appearance in Sekaori form. Why? Why not just Sekai? Is this an effort to segregate the spirit Sekai from Sekaori, the physical representation of Sekai's lingering influence through the unexplained linkage between her and Kaori? Is the latter one THE only one involved in divine chess games while the former is NOT?

Yeesh.
Honestly when chika was angry she was very rational. Reasonable accusations, some awareness of her own delusions, and grilling sensei for all the right reasons. But then something tripped and she started to reconstruct her perfect dream relationship out of her very imperfect reality.
Yumi has tried to get her to see how much of a scumbag Sensei is for a while. Now even Sensei is trying to get her to see how much he sucks and it fails.
It's clear at this point that Chika's delusions aren't because she's stupid but because she simply really really really doesn't want to lose that happy life of hers.
+1000 Affection, my god. In later events Sensei says Chika is currently more at risk of killing classmates than Ami and I'm inclined to agree.

Shout out to Yumi for being a good friend though. I know a lot of people are praying for her to break but it's nice seeing someone put their friend first when nearly every other roommate pair has progressed to active competition.

Did... Sana just re-kill her brother? I think knife-boy ceasing to be after losing his knives might have some implications for the nature of supernatural beings but without anything concrete I can't bring myself to think too much about it.

idk.
Event is weird as expected.

but unironically
Osako keeps getting these strangely intimate/familiar moments with Sensei.
I like these details in a scene. Maybe the reason we see them with Osako is because Sensei has always felt especially comfortable with her? Osako shuts down the possibility of being another conquest, she's both completely uninterested and capable of defending herself. Sensei says it's nice being with someone without the risk of another complicated affair. That might help him relax. She's like the male friend Sensei never had and for that reason I think Osako might be more important to him than people give her credit for. They're still not very close yet though.

The flashback was cute. Seeing how much that meant to Wakana is reassuring for their relationship. Maybe it will work out?

Behold, the realistic consequences of having 10 inches, porn be damned.

Sensei has this reoccurring self-destructive desire to receive justice that pops up multiple times here. First, Makoto talks him out of confessing to Maki but the mounting evidence should make Maki more than suspicious. So that will probably be a thing.
Second, he wants to be lectured by Makoto who then reveals her surprisingly thought-out careless outlook on life without time. I don't buy this outlook and Sensei is also hesitant to accept it.
Makoto's philosophy might be a necessary strategy to cope in an environment that could otherwise drive her insane.
The update was sort of all over the place, but that's not bad. We're in between major events and many story lines are just coasting until the next major happening while others are independantly entertaining scenes. I liked it overall.

spoilers.title: Osako
spoilers.html:
Osako keeps getting these strangely intimate/familiar moments with Sensei.
I like these details in a scene. Maybe the reason we see them with Osako is because Sensei has always felt especially comfortable with her? Osako shuts down the possibility of being another conquest, she's both completely uninterested and capable of defending herself. Sensei says it's nice being with someone without the risk of another complicated affair. That might help him relax. She's like the male friend Sensei never had and for that reason I think Osako might be more important to him than people give her credit for. They're still not very close yet though.

spoilers.title: Miku/Makoto
spoilers.html:
Behold, the realistic consequences of having 10 inches, porn be damned.
Kudos for having a responsible response. I was worried Sensei would just keep going.
Sensei has this reoccurring self-destructive desire to receive justice that pops up multiple times here. First, Makoto talks him out of confessing to Maki but the mounting evidence should make Maki more than suspicious. So that will probably be a thing.
Second, he wants to be lectured by Makoto who then reveals her surprisingly thought-out careless outlook on life without time. I don't buy this outlook and Sensei is also hesitant to accept it.
Makoto's philosophy might be a necessary strategy to cope in an environment that could otherwise drive her insane.

Update complete. I am in awe--You guys are all super fast with the analysis. I already gave some Chika thoughts but there's a lot of things happening here.

A fragile light thinking it will go out any moment, placed in a world where it never will. Yet that comforting truth is out of reach by the laws of the world.
Trying to prepare her loved ones for a time that will never come.

Seeing Chinami struggling to preserve her little family caused emotions.
Also, Chinami switching to first person speech throws me through a loop. She knows exactly what she's doing (GoT betrays us yet again). Clever girl.
She was doing so well but some people don't think they deserve happiness. (>.> looking at you sensei)
At least Sara knows how to approach her bs. Does Yumi know her mother's relapsing? Because Yumi's suffering quota still needs filling and that would do it.
Suddenly becoming the onee-sama was a big shift lol. She's a good friend. And an exhibitionist apparently.
She was surprisingly ok with being found out by Tsubasa. Maki would be proud. Haruka would be mad (that only Sara got away with it).
damn Tsubasa, you scary! And horny.
But the multiple foursomes are probably exaggerated to toy with Akira. Truly she is a master of seduction.

I agree that Tsubasa must have known Sekai in some way. Related? A hardcore fan? She got "Aki-kun" from somewhere. All that talk about fate sure is ominous.

As for the Tsubasa-Chosokabe connection:
I don't think Tsubasa was responsible for helping Chinami get treatment. She is far too hands on to let things deteriorate like they did. Unless there was some sort of falling out between her and Chiaki. But that wouldn't stop her, she would just use a cat's-paw.
So she might have known Chiaki, but probably did not know her circumstances.
Actually, how has Chika been paying for the treatment?
The horny is strong with her, but girl has her eye(s) on the prize: asking whether the spirits can make her best girl and force everyone else to give up. That takes cajones. Or maybe this is just revenge for all the times Ayane defiled her bed.
Still awkward. Not sure how Karin's arc will resolve. Maybe she has to push Akira down and have her way with him?
Cute hair style. Total breakup move tho. And seeing her give into peer pressure and join the MILF of the month club just showcased her innate sub nature. At least she and Akira and forming an actual relationshp. Which is good because his magnetic cock will draw her in even faster with proximity.
Seeing Wakana lean into her Akira friendship was cute. Now with hugging rights! It makes me wonder what their relationship was like pre-amnesia.
Rough first time. Can she recover from this and have a much better second time? (yes)
And her date with Akira was so cute before that.
Teacher's pet showcasing her new moral framework to accommodate an endless expanse of time. Of course, it's not perfect. I think one of the big issues is that previous Akira's didn't think things through and treated the loops as if they were completely independent. Which they are not, given leaky memories and autopilot actions.

In other words, there are (some) consequences to action, just not from external authorities. And Makoto's right in that typical views on morals and ethics don't apply. There is an inherent disconnect between appearance and truth.

Maybe only the good ol' "be excellent to each other" works here. Either way, Akira's moral compass is adjusting.

Overall, I thought it was a good update. Lots of fodder for speculation.

posts.content_html_raw:
Before this update I was in hard denial about Tsubasa having any sort of association with Sekai. These two smart and manipulative women might speak in similar manners that are too uncanny to ignore, but at the end of the day, these phrases alone to me weren't unique, obsolete, or out of place enough to patent them so that all who used such phrases would be registered under the same banner.
(I said that, but many sentences Tsubasa said this time had me on high alert; things like "It can change the way you perceive it", "We all look differently when we're hit by the light in certain ways", "Everything changes with the light", or "Sometimes, the things you see aren't really there." It almost feels like Tsubasa is secretly a follower of Yasu's religion or something.)

But now, purposefully stringing what she said in a particular manner can pave the way for her to potentially get acquainted with Sekai via normal means. Particularly, the "You remind me of an old friend when you get passionate like that, then the use of "Aki-kun" that triggered the said passion. The whole defining his negative responses as passion under the right light is so unsettling that I can't ignore the similarity in mindset, and I am willing to think that Tsubasa doesn't just become this due to being a caged bird, but due to being under a certain bad influence.

There is still a few percent of me believe that calling him "Aki-kun" is all but serendipitous (as in, from "Akira" to "Aki-kun" isn't all that dumbfounded). But Tsubasa didn't flinch at all when Akira responded with strong negative emotions and continued her provoking; so a bigger percent of me believe calling him that was a deliberate move and that, her knowing the real reason why Sensei disliked that pet name, would mean a multitude of things. Currently the only one that knows how "Aki-kun" works is Nodoka and she scienced that shit out almost like a psychic with her otherworldly brain. I can't find other means for Tsubasa to know this other than Sekai telling her herself years later. The hole in this theory is that I think Tusbasa should've known all these as early as The Lucky Few but she didn't give me that feeling in that event.

Even if I scratch all of these headcanons and treat them as forging connections when there is none, the reason why I go all in this time on Sekai is that there isn't really anyone else that feels remotely close to the depiction, especially the passionate part.
- Wakana: They became acquainted only after Playing God. Plus, Tsubasa should've just addressed her name instead of being this vague in front of Akira if it WAS Wakana.
- Chiaki: I don't see a conceivable path that led them to meet, and led Tsubasa to care enough for Chiaki's situation. Besides, Tsubasa never needed to commit health insurance fraud when she could literally buy the entire hospital like it was nothing. It'd also make Curry Night continuity very weird.

- The rest(?): Tsubasa knew too few people that could be relevant in this case, and I'd be very disappointed if this old friend being someone entirely not introduced yet, but I'd love to consider some other strong candidates for this old friend position if anyone can refer more.

posts.content_html_raw:
Here's some rambling ideas about Makoto's "T Is For Time". I don't have a complete theory so I basically just started pointing out every connection that might be relevant, hopefully this can spark a discussion.
For me, Friedrich Nietzsche Makoto's arguments come across as dangerously persuasive but ultimately bullshit, and I hope that's what Selebus is intending. You can probably apply the mental maturity argument to Maya Prime, though there are still caveats with how underdeveloped teenage brains are, but every one of Sensei's sexual relationships started within months of the girl being reset and at most within a few years of them being factory reset, so I don't know how they can be said to have matured (and they don't act like it).

If this really was Makoto, I would love to see how her newfound philosophy stands up to learning about the wizards. "No babe, it's just like you said! It's totally okay for me to be fucking the girl in the dog mask because mentally she's actually lived through thousands of years! She's so mature that sometimes she even speaks in the first person!"

The idea that morality doesn't matter when everything is going to be reset anyway also doesn't hold any water. As Maya Prime would say, these are real people he's hurting.
To carry Makoto's argument to the limits of absurdity, it's obviously not okay to assault an amnesiac just because they'll eventually forget about it, and I don't see how the resets are any different. I think Makoto's first event in 0.43 is actually a great illustration of this. Makoto might have consented to being assaulted in her sleep if she knew about it, but she didn't. There are no consequences except for an awkward sex dream because she doesn't realize what Sensei did. But that doesn't make raping her any less morally objectionable.

As Moonflare pointed out, although the arguments are different, the end results of what Makoto is suggesting would be the same as what Sekai/Pareidolia want Sensei to do: stop looking for answers, accept your "true self" that doesn't care about doing the right thing, and just enjoy fucking girls who can at best questionably consent.
No. Thank you for coming to my TED Talk.












But seriously, I really don't think this is Makoto talking. Everything just feels somewhat off, little things like reassuring Sensei that he's not as bad as he thinks he is when in the past it was she who always reminded him what a terrible person he is. But for me the real giveaway is the "I love you so much".
Even when Sensei said it first, I don't think Makoto has ever directly admitted to loving him, much less gushed about it in this way. And saying she's lucky to be able to live forever is a remarkable turnaround from the girl who wants to kill herself but decided she'll live just so others won't suffer from her death.

Let's look at some of the language she uses:
This is remarkably similar to what the narrator said in "Rewrite" back during the first reset:
I don't think this is coincidence, whoever is speaking as Makoto here is supposed to the same as the narrator of "Rewrite". Unfortunately, I'm not sure who that is: Sekai, Maya, and Ami all seem to have points in their favor, but they also each have significant problems.
"Rewrite" is the event where the narrator introduces the story of Nozomu, the horny ball of light. Even if you disagree with me that it's relevant to "T Is For Time", I think the question of who narrates this event is really perplexing.

...
Points for Ami as narrator:
  • She says "I love you so much" to Sensei all the time.
  • During Sensei's Chapter 4 breakdown, she talks about the two of them running away again so it'll be only the two of them like it's meant to be.
  • Upside down Ami in "Trinity Pt. I" talks about rewriting the world, though she says only God has that ability.
  • The narrator's casual tone and the ditziness of the Van Gogh question matches her personality.
Problems with Ami:
  • The narrator's outlook is a lot more cynical than Ami's, and in particular Ami believes in God and has a positive attitude toward him.
Points for Sekai:
  • She also tends to say "I love you so much".
    ...
    ...
  • The cynicism, disdain for God (especially one named Nozomu), and focus on sex all match her general attitude.
  • The references to "our children" might be literal if Ami is Akira's daughter.
Problems with Sekai:
  • The narrator says that "we're approaching death", implying that they're still alive and mortal.
  • Would Sekai really talk about how it's always been "just you and me"? Surely she would include Ami as well.
Points for Maya:
  • The declaration that God is dead is echoed by Maya in "Trinity Pt. I" and the crying AmIOkay in "The Room With Clocks".
  • I think Maya has already narrated events earlier in the chapter.
  • Maya wants to fix the world.
Problems with Maya:
  • The tone just sounds all wrong, far too casual and profane, and Maya wouldn't be going on tangents about Van Gogh.
  • I don't think that she could/would claim that it's always been "just you and me" when Ami has always been in the picture and even New Maya says that she cares about two people (RIP Ayane).
Beyond these three I can't see anyone else who could make the slightest claim to "it's always been just you and me". If you put a gun to my head I'm probably guessing that the narrator is Sekai, but I'm not happy about it.
Sensei specifically points out that he recognizes the cat, which makes me think it is supposed to be significant.

Here's my current read on what pre-loop Akira was like. I'm filling in gaps so lot of this is speculation and it's a kinda rambly wall of text so feel free to ignore.
Akira both loved and resented Sekai. He was a confused and troubled kid who needed help. Sekai was that help but eventually she abused her position and groomed/molested him. Literature and poetry became therapeutic as it explored different perspectives and feelings that Akira could connect to in lieu of a proper mentor. Having a lot of trouble at home, Akira spent much of his time at Niki's house to escape his brother, mother, and/or sekai.
Akira's experiences gave him a soft spot for broken people. This is what spurred him to try to be the teacher he never had, one that would help young people rather than abuse them. Eventually he got into tutoring.

Then, of course Sekai dies and Akira breaks. Akira stops talking to Niki either because spending time with his other girlfriend after the last one died feels like a betrayal, or he doesn't feel he can open up to Niki so he runs away. At this point I don't believe Akira intends to cut Niki out forever. He just needs some time.

He becomes Ami's guardian. Ami starts out as a reminder of that terrible/wonderful person Akira lost. She's an innocent girl who is the target of Akira internal thoughts of love, hate, longing, and grief. Eventually Ami starts taking care of the two of them and finds purpose and companionship in Akira.

Akira goes back to tutoring. Ghost Sekai isn't real yet but her memory is haunting him. Teaching is almost a form of protest to Akira. A rebuttal to Sekai's methods. Akira discovers Maya, a homeless girl who sets off his help-young-people instinct. He shelters her at his old apartment where he tutors and starts educating her as well. In his mind, this will be a demonstration of what a proper mentor should be. Not just to sekai's memory but to himself as he is feeling temptation.
He is in a lot of situations where he is alone with young girls. Ami has started bringing Ayane home and Akira teaches both Noriko and Maya. Everywhere he goes he has an opportunity for abuse, an opportunity to be like Sekai. But he's determined to be a good person in spite of what sekai was. His resolve does not falter but the thoughts don't leave him either.
Maya starts to see cracks and begins to entertain a relationship. She is desensitized to being with an adult due to her experiences during/before homelessness so her affection starts to fester.

Eventually Akira has a blackout and Maya takes advantage of this. Akira crosses a line he didn't want to cross. They have a conversation and conclude that they are messed up broken people who can fix one another. They become an item. The silver lining is that Maya can be a sexual outlet for Akira. He can be a more secure person for his students, Ayane and maybe Ami(if good/bad uncle is a thing) because of Maya. Maya's nack for acting and roleplay support this.
But the biggest casualty here is that he can't go back to Niki now which is why the Nakayamas get cut off completely.

So yeah. If you take this equation and subtract Maya and Akira's memories/resolve you basically get current loop Sensei.

Noriko reveals a lot about Maya, but one of the major things is how she believes Maya fucked Sensei up for good:
View attachment 3339022 Noriko - "No, what I should have done is never let you take advantage of him. Because that fucked him up for good. And I think you know it."

As far as has been revealed, Maya was the one who pursued the relationship with Sensei:
View attachment 3339028 Presumably Maya - "do you remember the first time you told me you loved me? it was snowing. i was wearing a green scarf. i confessed my feelings to you weeks prior and you had been sitting on your decision ever since. when you uttered those words, it was like my heart stopped. like everything i've ever wanted was finally mine. and i could finally be happy. you took me to your room and took my panties off. you put your fingers inside me and i started crying. but they were happy tears - because I finally knew what it meant to be loved."

We also had Pareidolia seemingly disliking Maya for how she groomed Sensei:
View attachment 3339035 Pareidolia - "Not the person she wanted you to be. Not the person she groomed you into --- a broken man incapable of dividing what little love he has left into boxes to share with everyone and everything."

And we know that Maya tried to keep those that loved Sensei away from him, apparently convincing him he was all alone:
View attachment 3339038 View attachment 3339039 View attachment 3339040 View attachment 3339042 Noriko - "What you don't do is hide them from everyone else who cares about them and make them think they're all alone! That is being obsessed, Maya!"
Maya - "You should thank me for keeping her away as long as I have."
Sensei - "How were you the one who kept her away?"
Maya - "That doesn't concern you."

We also had Sensei mentioning he was willing to be Maya's toy last update:
View attachment 3339274 View attachment 3339269 View attachment 3339270 View attachment 3339272 Ami - "Maya never cared about you. And she never will care about you because she's a filthy liar who manipulates people into doing what she wants them to do. Plus, she-"
- "Plus, she's changed a lot these last couple months. I guess her true colors are really coming out now that her favorite toy has been taken away."
Sensei - "I will be a toy if it means..."
Ami - "You will do nothing of the sort. Your brain is going haywire right now and you're saying things you don't mean. But that's my fault for leaving you alone in a place where people can find you."

And, Ami has brought up that she suspects something must have hurt Sensei to cause him to stop tutoring:
View attachment 3339336 View attachment 3339338 Ami - "I'm sure it's not true, but I keep thinking that maybe something happened with you while I wasn't around that hurt you really bad."
- "Because, somewhere along the line, you gave up on tutoring. And I never really understood why."

It seems like the only thing that could have hurt him, and the main thing that sends his body into shock, is him remembering his relationship with Maya.

As fucked up as it sounds, it seems like a Wizard took advantage of a mentally ill man in his 20s, and broke him into his modern self in his early 30s.

Overall: Sekai probably dislikes Maya for what Maya did to Sensei mentally.

Not to mention, if Sekai is just some kind of hallucination from Sensei's mind, it might be the part of Sensei that regrets and dislikes what he did with Maya, personified. Just, you know, blaming the Wizard.

Chika's delusion arc is objectively being dragged on for too long. I get the feeling that Sel has been struggling with fitting everything into the right timeline, her "waking up" has been long overdue and there were many opportunities before to introduce her downfall, in my opinion.

With Miku's latest scene being something that Sel admitted he planned since Chapter 1 that ended up in Chapter 4, apparently meant as a shocker, I feel like he is starting to get things slightly out of a logical order. That scene would indeed have a big impact, I believe, if it happened somewhere in Chatper 2 or 3. I don't remember who it was but someone (with a bigger noggin than me) mentioned that the first scene with Miku panicking was potentially planned as being the first sex scene and thus basically this event, but got changed during development. It would make sense, given that Stomachache happened (which I haven't watched yet myself but I understand the gist of what has happened, I guess, shut up don't judge me) in the meantime, which is kind of dwarfing the impact of Miku's scene now.

The same would apply to Maki's refusal to even consider Akira's involvement in Makoto's and now Miku's sex life. Maki may be a little weird, but she is smart, obviously she would have at least started to sniff out that Akira might be more than just friends with her two daughters, but there has been nothing so far that would indicate that, as far as I know.
Similarly Niki, who seems a little too oblivious to everything as well (though I play the good uncle route so I did not have the cum jar scene, but that means its not canon then ).

It makes me wonder whether Sel was deliberately stalling some of the developments to put them closer to the dark routes and have a more significant transition into what would become the switch from harem to dark.
Who knows what he has planned, but I could imagine it being a culmination of characters having their "eyes opened" and seeing the "true" Akira all in close timely proximity to each other, cascading into a series of events that exponentially develop into a huge pile of problemburgers for Akira that eventually initiate said dark route. Hence, from Sel's perspective, he didn't want some of those revelation to happen too early in the timeline, I guess?
Still, to me it seems a little off and illogical for most of the characters. Not a huge issue, but still a gripe I have with some of the current developments. And maybe it will make sense over time, who knows.

I think people are ascribing too much agency to Maya in her relationship with Sensei. She was seven years old, I'm going to need a whole mound of compelling direct evidence before I believe that she was the instigator or driver of a sexual relationship with an adult, and even then the first assumption should be that she was groomed into it. I think, if anything, the scarf story even points against it. It was Sensei that fingered her, all she did was confess her love (again, the love of a seven-year-old).
Moonflare said:
Which one? Noriko insists someone (assumed to be Maya) did something to/with Akira in the Old District after he ghosted her, and she saw him from the bus. One theory is that Maya made out with him in public or something, in an effort to make him leave the old district for good - but that's a very steep shot in the dark at this point (this happens during her first conversation with Akira about the past, in which he starts to shut down).

The other time Noriko mentions something related to this is directly to Maya, but that's more about the fact that she had sex with him while being a kid, putting him on a road of no return, and that she knows that Maya also knows she ruined him by doing it. Which is totally true. There'd be no person not sympathetic to Akira if not for the Maya situation - up until that point he was 100% just a victim of a horrible person, and there is a strong hint that this act was in part pragmatism from Maya's end to cut him off from everyone else as well (New Maya jokes about calling the police if he doesn't have sex with her, and at some point this might have been actual blackmail - if he didn't leave Noriko/Niki/the Old District).
Click to expand...
I don't have an explanation for Noriko's story, but I'm not convinced that it's Maya that she saw. According to the pact they made as kids, Maya can't go to the old district, yet both of them seem to agree that it was Noriko who broke the pact in the present day. If Noriko saw Maya in the old district, surely she would bring that up.
As a side note, I still don't understand what Noriko was supposed to get out of that pact. Even if she was a kid and didn't understand the implications, she must have agreed to it for a reason.
I don't think Maya kissing him in public makes much sense. It's not like the old and new districts are completely separate worlds. If he's at risk of being recognized and unmasked in the old district, that risk would still exist elsewhere in the city even if it's less.

New Maya mentioning the police came across to me as a sex kink thing, since Sensei gets off on how taboo his relationships are. I don't think there was any indication that it was an actual threat or that she had threatened it before.
DeSkel15 said:
Noriko does imply that Maya is the one who fucked Sensei up for good:
View attachment 3998062 Noriko - "No, what I should have done is never let you take advantage of him. Because that fucked him up for good. And I think you know it."
(Chapter 3 'Flowerchild' Main Event)

Mentioned it before:

But it does seem like within months of Sekai's death, Wizard Maya had Sensei wrapped around her finger, and Niki was out of the picture.
Click to expand...
As this thread's resident Noriko hater, I feel obligated to push back on some of this. To start with, Noriko is not an objective source when it comes to Maya. Her feelings towards her are all kinds of confused, but they include jealousy and bearing a grudge over the past.
More importantly, there's a lot of stuff that Noriko doesn't know about. She doesn't know about Sensei's relationship with Sekai, which was probably a big impetus for why he had to leave the old district. She doesn't know anything about what happened between when he left and when she joined the class. She sees that he's even more broken now than she remembers, so she blames Maya for that, but up until whatever triggered the resets, it seems like he had actually improved significantly outside of having an underage girlfriend.

In context, what she actually blames Maya for is not fixing him, but she doesn't know that the resets made that impossible.
Maya isn't responsible for Sensei ghosting Niki, that happened immediately after the accident when he holed up in his house with Ami. After he started improving and leaving the house, he still chose to avoid her. Even Noriko doesn't blame Maya for him abandoning them the first time.
It's reasonable to argue that Sensei would have eventually let Niki back into his life if Maya didn't push him away, but there isn't any evidence that he was considering it. I think it's telling that Sensei never talked about the Nakayamas with Ami.

As far as I'm concerned, the only thing that Maya was guilty of was pushing Sensei to leave Noriko and the old district behind. Even then, she thinks she had a good reason for it, though I'm sure her selfishness and jealousy played a large part.

...
It's also worth pointing out that we still have no idea why Maya hates Noriko so much, and Noriko clearly doesn't know either since she thinks it's for loving Sensei, which she realizes makes no sense.
I can't see Maya Prime maintaining this hatred for thousands of years unless either: 1. Noriko has been showing up during resets (and Maya lied about it). or 2. Maya blames her for some aspect of Sensei's present condition.
Moonflare said:
Edit: Last possible reason is half tinfoil, but it could be that she hates Maya because they're both pursuing different goals reset wise. They're the top narrator guesses after Himawari, and her hatred could be a "present" hate, born during the resets, and for supernatural reasons - rather than the hate of the memory of a dead person looking over someone that wasn't even part of Akira's life when she was alive.
Click to expand...
I'd actually argue that this is the only reason that we have direct evidence for. Sekai and Pareidolia view Sensei being broken as his true self, and they want him to return to that and become the Collector. Maya Prime was pushing him in the opposite direction, trying to get him to care about the girls. When Pareidolia talks about Maya grooming Sensei, he's referring to what she's done during the resets, not to their sexual relationship.

When Pareidolia talks about Maya grooming Sensei, he's referring to what she's done during the resets, not to their sexual relationship.
Spoiler
View attachment 4000710
View attachment 4000712
View attachment 4000715
Click to expand...
Sensei likely wasn't allowed to bring up the Nakayamas. Maya seemed to make it part of their relationship, at least when it came to Niki:
Spoiler
Maya - "What do you mean I'm not 'her?' And which 'her' are you talking about in the first place since we agreed not to talk about
either
of them?"
(Chapter 4 Maya 'Miraculous Human-Glue' Event)
Sensei - "If I tell you it's because of Niki, will that be enough to make you leave?"
Maya - "D..."
- "Don't even joke about that..."
- "You
know
how I feel about her. And we agreed that we wouldn't-"
(Chapter 4 Maya 'Radio Silence' Event)
The Nakayamas plus Sekai seemed to be the only three people Maya was jealous of:
Spoiler
Narrator - "Her
actual
jealousy was focused at three other people. But, on the bright side, one of those people were dead."
- "But two of them weren't."
- "And one of them just so happens to be the
real
subject for event numero dos."
(Chapter 4 Noriko 'Rivals (Taco Tuesday)' Event)
And were likely treated as taboo to even think about within their relationship since the start.
If Sensei's selective "amnesia" wasn't already a thing by that time, he simply wasn't allowed to mention the Nakayamas and definitely wouldn't be allowed to make them part of Ami's life.
Noriko also specifically blames Maya for making Sensei think he's all alone:
Spoiler
Noriko - "What you
don't
do is hide them from everyone else who cares about them and make them think they're all alone!
That
is being obsessed, Maya!"
(Chapter 3 'Flowerchild' Main Event)
And we know that even Maya Prime, after possibly millions of years from her perspective, was still hiding Noriko from him.
When it comes to Noriko and Maya, it really does just seem to come down to Maya's jealousy and obsessiveness. Even if she's trying to justify it. (Although, I have wondered if Maya thought that Noriko was the wizard he
truly
wanted, but held himself back due to "love" and fear. Him seeing Tsukasa as wizard Noriko is...interesting. I don't think Maya would have liked being called "Noriko" when they were messing around, or at all.)
Also keep in mind that Noriko, even after everything, still cares about Maya:
Spoiler
Noriko - "Maya, as much as you hate me, I care about you. And even if there's an earth-shattering rivalry between us, I don't actually want to hurt you. I want you to be happy."
She's not aware of everything, but it's not like she's trying to slander Maya, when she's connecting the dots.
There's definitely more to the Maya/Niki stuff though, as Niki seemed to recognize Maya:
Spoiler
Niki - "Something just felt kind of...
off
about her. Like I recognize her from somewhere or..."
(Chapter 4 'When the Sun Sleeps' Main Event)
But we probably won't know
what,
until Maya finds out that she's moving in and the real drama starts. Still probably just comes down to jealousy, and Maya Prime was notably the most jealous of Niki according to the Chapter 3 'Untitled' Main Event.
Don't get me wrong though. Even if Maya instigated this relationship, it is still Sensei who's to blame for it's existence and it being sexual. His
weakness
does not and will not excuse his actions as far as I'm concerned.
-----
As for who Noriko saw with Sensei in the Old District: I'm thinking it may have been Ami on a day they went to visit Sekai's grave or her old house in the Old District. Something along those lines.
It kind of has to be either Ami or Maya, and it definitely doesn't fit Maya, after the pact was revealed, but something made him feel something he didn't like remembering based off him hallucinating.
Edit: Also Pareidolia is bringing up Sekai (probably), Maya, and Sensei's Parents in that Chapter 4 'The Collector' Main Event. It only referring to what happened in the Resets seems unlikely.

posts.content_html_raw:
barglenarglezous said:
I'm honestly of a mind to say that whenever any given character is speaking about another character's past or motives, to assume the speaker is unreliable. Bias and agendas are abundant here, and just because a character says something (even when well-intentioned) doesn't mean they actually know what they're talking about. Especially where the memory of children is involved.
Click to expand...
I agree to an extent, but there is a danger in this sort of story where so much is already unreliable to make your reader view things people straight up reveal as unreliable as well. One might end up falling into a sort of solipsism of meaning where you can only trust what you see, but since Akira isn't realiable either then there's no meaning to be found anywhere.

I'd go with assuming people having an agenda and biases to what they say, rather than straight up lying (unless it's hinted that they are). For instance, I don't think Noriko lied once about what she said about the past/Maya. Whereas I know for sure Maya lied a lot, and might have hid even more information.

There is a final piece to this in that they're not real people. Selebus chose to tell his story through unreliable means, but on the same token, all characters are mediums to one single narrator which is himself - so all of them know what they're talking about when he wishes them to know what they're talking about - in order to convey to the reader another fragment of the lore when it's appropriate. I personally haven't found much misinformation that was conveyed through characters about other characters that I recall (not ones that weren't apparent they're just guesses from the start at least).

posts.content_html_raw:
Some thoughts on the Yumi & Chika events that ended up way longer than I thought they would. So ill put them in a spoiler tag so they wont be a waste of space in the event that they don't contain anything worth reading.
Either I'm far too Yumi pilled, or Chika did actually break Yuim’s heart in their event. I honestly somehow felt my own heart break as if it were her’s. And the worst part is she will end up at least partly blaming herself. I also can't help but treat Yuki’s state of mind as a lens or window into what a broken Yumi can become. I read a hopelessness or despair somewhat similar to Yuki’s coming from Yumi at the end of the event. Godspeed Noriko, you might be the only one that can actually catch her fall now.

Additional Chika does seem to have undergone a somewhat major change in the nature of her delusion. You can tell mostly from the fact that at the end she treats needing to apologise to Yumi as an afterthought to whatever the hell she came up with regarding her and Akira’s relationship. She really did tell Yumi, the girl she surely knows is afraid of making any emotional connections because of her mother abandoning her and being raised in a Yakuza den, who presumably saw people have their connections used against them on a regular basis. That even having some desire to finally connect with or rely on someone else, and not even acting on that desire, is somehow unforgivable.

She has in a way just killed her, or attest broke the only place she felt comfortable. One of only 2 people in the world Yumi cared about (the other being Chinami) was the one to throw her away like trash. All over a man far more suited to the company of trash than either of the girls. That will devastate Yumi. Chika should know that, yet did not even seem to care. Perhaps somewhat like those Yakuza Yumi grew up around. She cut Yumi to pieces without a second thought. More willing to believe her delusions than the one girl who would never want to hurt her.

Chika: “You aren't welcome here anymore… I just don't want you here anymore…a spineless, backstabbing, self-serving bitch… taking advantage of our kindness for too long. So she's not welcome anymore… You were like a sister to me(past tense)... I love him… in a way you never could…you probably begged for it… This shit is unforgivable, Yumi… we can't all be aloof and heartless lone wolves like you…”

Yumi: “It seems like you’ve already made up your mind about how much I fucking suck. – I never meant to hurt you, Chika. – I just aint good at having feelings.”

She aint good at having feelings? She is far better at it than Chika this time. But somehow she will internalise that her feelings are wrong. That they are what caused this. That she is the problem. That if she just kept her armour up, and never let it crack, that somehow It would have prevented this. That somehow Chika's inability to ever listen to her every time she tried to tell her anything about Akira is because she is that one that “ain't good at having feelings”.

I do think Yumi will forgive her words. But I am not sure Rabid-Chika will even be able to notice her falling. And Akira would probably just unintentionally drag Yumi down with him. So Noriko might be her only hope. Yumi always wanted someone she could trust enough to lean on at times like this. As close as she was to Chika, she never truly could without feeling like a burden. Now even that is gone. She might go to Yuki, she will probably find out about her recent developments… Then that will leave Noriko to come in and scoop her up off the ground with a well timed hug. Crack her open like an egg. And finding out once and for all, that all the king horses and all the king's men were really just a bunch of bumbling buffoons... Whatever happens, I just hope that “Egg Boy”, is not allowed to get “at it again”. Anywhere near her for the time being.

I guess we also have the 1000 affection points that are a clear indicator of a big change in Chika and that something bad is about to happen. There is no way Selebus gives her those points without the intention of taking them and maybe even more away.

And finally, perhaps if I am in fact, far too Yumi pilled, maybe none of that even happened. Maybe most of it is a projection of my own mind’s making onto Yumi, and thus Chika's characters. I'll leave that for you to decide because I'm clearly traped between the lines. But I can't really be bothered to discuss if my rambling thoughts do or do not align with anyone else's on this. And I do quite enjoy the extra pain they bring me. So I shall respectfully and pre-emptively agree to disagree with anyone that might take a different reading of it.

There's nothing that I really disagree with on the emotional level, so you can just take that and disregard whatever I'm going to say right now. I mean, I've been pretty vocal against Chika's current arc and on how much I love Yumi and her development through multiple posts...

That being said, Chika's reaction is perfectly understandable and logical imo (as it concerns Yumi's event). Her own event is where I think Selebus drops the ball.

So hey, here comes Chika's greatest critic to her defense this time: Chika has told Yumi a hundred times that it was obvious she liked Akira. She has tried having an honest talk with her, she has tried cucking her, she might have even tried inviting her to a threesome. Most important of all, Chika has told Yumi no cap that if Yumi didn't come clear with her feelings, it was bound to blow up in their faces and it would ruin their relationship.

That's what happened. What Chika saw, even though on the surface was a misunderstanding, at the core it very much wasn't and she says so this during this last update. Yes, Akira wasn't cheating on her with Yumi, and neither they went back to their bedroom to have sex. She was wrong about that.

But what she was not wrong about is that they both were lost in eachother's eyes in a manner that just wasn't ever true with her. That Yumi was not coerced into that situation and that she wanted to kiss him back. That she has for a long time. That she let this blow up in Chika's face when she could have very easily just said so for years now.

Now, is part of this Chika's fault for not listening to the so many people that tried to open her eyes (Akira included)? Yes, 100%. But her reaction is still valid, because if we look to another example of surrogate sisters, Miku didn't wait a single day to tell Makoto she kissed Akira and to apologise.

This is guesswork, but if Yumi were to come clean with Chika before she confronted her, I think this would have gone down very differently. She didn't, in a huge part because Chika is insane. And in a smaller one because nothing really happened from her perspective.

But, and that is the point of this post, Chika has every right to lose her cool with Yumi. I wouldn't blame her at all on that front to be honest, she'll probably apologise for the things she got wrong, and when she does, the things she got right will more than compensate for the emotional distress of the rest. Yumi has fucked up, she has feelings for him and she let herself be in that situation with her sister's boyfriend.

If Chika didn't see it, it would have been fine. But now that she saw it, there's a whole arc of things she didn't see that become evident to her. They didn't get to that point from zero, and it's all been going on behind her back, and even before they were a thing, with Yumi keeping all that a secret from her (while she asked her about it many times over).

But her reaction is still valid, because if we look to another example of surrogate sisters, Miku didn't wait a single day to tell Makoto she kissed Akira and to apologise.
This is guesswork, but if Yumi were to come clean with Chika before she confronted her, I think this would have gone down very differently. She didn't, in a huge part because Chika is insane.  And in a smaller one because nothing really happened from her perspective.
But, and that is the point of this post, Chika has every right to lose her cool with Yumi. I wouldn't blame her at all on that front to be honest, she'll probably apologise for the things she got wrong, and when she does, the things she got right will more than compensate for the emotional distress of the rest. Yumi has fucked up, she has feelings for him and she let herself be in that situation with her sister's boyfriend.
If Chika didn't see it, it would have been fine. But now that she saw it, there's a whole arc of things she didn't see that become evident to her. They didn't get to that point from zero, and it's all been going on behind her back, and even before they were a thing, with Yumi keeping all that a secret from her (while she asked her about it many times over).

spoilers.title: Yumi, Chika, thoughts, maybe too long, maybe not long enough.
spoilers.html:
Either I'm far too Yumi pilled, or Chika did actually break Yuim’s heart in their event. I honestly somehow felt my own heart break as if it were her’s. And the worst part is she will end up at least partly blaming herself. I also can't help but treat Yuki’s state of mind as a lens or window into what a broken Yumi can become. I read a hopelessness or despair somewhat similar to Yuki’s coming from Yumi at the end of the event. Godspeed Noriko, you might be the only one that can actually catch her fall now.

Additional Chika does seem to have undergone a somewhat major change in the nature of her delusion. You can tell mostly from the fact that at the end she treats needing to apologise to Yumi as an afterthought to whatever the hell she came up with regarding her and Akira’s relationship. She really did tell Yumi, the girl she surely knows is afraid of making any emotional connections because of her mother abandoning her and being raised in a Yakuza den, who presumably saw people have their connections used against them on a regular basis. That even having some desire to finally connect with or rely on someone else, and not even acting on that desire, is somehow unforgivable.

She has in a way just killed her, or attest broke the only place she felt comfortable. One of only 2 people in the world Yumi cared about (the other being Chinami) was the one to throw her away like trash. All over a man far more suited to the company of trash than either of the girls. That will devastate Yumi. Chika should know that, yet did not even seem to care. Perhaps somewhat like those Yakuza Yumi grew up around. She cut Yumi to pieces without a second thought. More willing to believe her delusions than the one girl who would never want to hurt her.

Chika: “You aren't welcome here anymore… I just don't want you here anymore…a spineless, backstabbing, self-serving bitch… taking advantage of our kindness for too long. So she's not welcome anymore… You were like a sister to me(past tense)... I love him… in a way you never could…you probably begged for it… This shit is unforgivable, Yumi… we can't all be aloof and heartless lone wolves like you…”

Yumi: “It seems like you’ve already made up your mind about how much I fucking suck. – I never meant to hurt you, Chika. – I just aint good at having feelings.”

She aint good at having feelings? She is far better at it than Chika this time. But somehow she will internalise that her feelings are wrong. That they are what caused this. That she is the problem. That if she just kept her armour up, and never let it crack, that somehow It would have prevented this. That somehow Chika's inability to ever listen to her every time she tried to tell her anything about Akira is because she is that one that “ain't good at having feelings”.

I do think Yumi will forgive her words. But I am not sure Rabid-Chika will even be able to notice her falling. And Akira would probably just unintentionally drag Yumi down with him. So Noriko might be her only hope. Yumi always wanted someone she could trust enough to lean on at times like this. As close as she was to Chika, she never truly could without feeling like a burden. Now even that is gone. She might go to Yuki, she will probably find out about her recent developments… Then that will leave Noriko to come in and scoop her up off the ground with a well timed hug. Crack her open like an egg. And finding out once and for all, that all the king horses and all the king's men were really just a bunch of bumbling buffoons... Whatever happens, I just hope that “Egg Boy”, is not allowed to get “at it again”. Anywhere near her for the time being.

I guess we also have the 1000 affection points that are a clear indicator of a big change in Chika and that something bad is about to happen. There is no way Selebus gives her those points without the intention of taking them and maybe even more away.

And finally, perhaps if I am in fact, far too Yumi pilled, maybe none of that even happened. Maybe most of it is a projection of my own mind’s making onto Yumi, and thus Chika's characters. I'll leave that for you to decide because I'm clearly traped between the lines. But I can't really be bothered to discuss if my rambling thoughts do or do not align with anyone else's on this. And I do quite enjoy the extra pain they bring me. So I shall respectfully and pre-emptively agree to disagree with anyone that might take a different reading of it.

Bingoogus said:
Man... it's really started to get to me, what with Selly saying it'll be the shortest chapter... like... all this fucking buildup to it coming and now it sounds like it'll start and end in like 6 updates or something... what a fucken disappointment, there's no way it's going to be worth it cause if it's not going to go on for a long while it's just going to be the teenage edgelord fanfic of the game before it all gets reset and the purity routes begin... seriously makes me wonder if Selly has written himself into a corner, all this great build up and no satisfying way to wrap it up...
Click to expand...
But, man, 6 updates is a long time... It might not seem that way right now, but I think that it was DeSkel that put it like this: how the hell is Selebus even going to extend the dark route's events? I mean, if it really is as dark as it's supposed to be, then it kind of has to be short-lived - otherwise we either change the genre to torture porn, or we have to turn LiL into an update long monologue as everyone's dead but Akira, and he's waiting for Godot/the reset.

There's no real point for 20 events back to back, over 6 months, when every single one of them is Stomachache. It'd be way too taxing on the readers and it would just stop being meaningful very fast.

If you instead think about the dark route as a sort of arc where everything that was setup during the harem arc gets triggered, then it makes sense that it's short - exactly because it's just triggering everything that was setup. What really takes time is either setting things up or closing them down. Harem sets them up, Purity closes them down. Dark route has to be short because it will neither set nothing up, nor close anything.

Or not, that's all guesswork. I personally don't much care for a "dark route" anyway. Sounds way too edgy, but that may also be just a tactic to not give out what it's about (it could actually be about regaining all memories of previous resets, and rather than bad things happening, it's about seeing the bad that already has idk). It could be a lot of things.

Moonflare said:
There's nothing that I really disagree with on the emotional level, so you can just take that and disregard whatever I'm going to say right now. I mean, I've been pretty vocal against Chika's current arc and on how much I love Yumi and her development through multiple posts...

That being said, Chika's reaction is perfectly understandable and logical imo (as it concerns Yumi's event). Her own event is where I think Selebus drops the ball.

So hey, here comes Chika's greatest critic to her defense this time: Chika has told Yumi a hundred times that it was obvious she liked Akira. She has tried having an honest talk with her, she has tried cucking her, she might have even tried inviting her to a threesome. Most important of all, Chika has told Yumi no cap that if Yumi didn't come clear with her feelings, it was bound to blow up in their faces and it would ruin their relationship.

That's what happened. What Chika saw, even though on the surface was a misunderstanding, at the core it very much wasn't and she says so this during this last update. Yes, Akira wasn't cheating on her with Yumi, and neither they went back to their bedroom to have sex. She was wrong about that.

But what she was not wrong about is that they both were lost in eachother's eyes in a manner that just wasn't ever true with her. That Yumi was not coerced into that situation and that she wanted to kiss him back. That she has for a long time. That she let this blow up in Chika's face when she could have very easily just said so for years now.

Now, is part of this Chika's fault for not listening to the so many people that tried to open her eyes (Akira included)? Yes, 100%. But her reaction is still valid, because if we look to another example of surrogate sisters, Miku didn't wait a single day to tell Makoto she kissed Akira and to apologise.

This is guesswork, but if Yumi were to come clean with Chika before she confronted her, I think this would have gone down very differently. She didn't, in a huge part because Chika is insane. And in a smaller one because nothing really happened from her perspective.

But, and that is the point of this post, Chika has every right to lose her cool with Yumi. I wouldn't blame her at all on that front to be honest, she'll probably apologise for the things she got wrong, and when she does, the things she got right will more than compensate for the emotional distress of the rest. Yumi has fucked up, she has feelings for him and she let herself be in that situation with her sister's boyfriend.

If Chika didn't see it, it would have been fine. But now that she saw it, there's a whole arc of things she didn't see that become evident to her. They didn't get to that point from zero, and it's all been going on behind her back, and even before they were a thing, with Yumi keeping all that a secret from her (while she asked her about it many times over).

And therein lies the issue with writing a story piecemeal and uploading it bit by bit - there's no editing of the story as a whole, no coherent vision from start to finish. Ideas and plot hooks get added, and forgotten, and dropped. Set ups are never knocked down, guns remain unfired because this month the author decides to change his vision.

Writing a story and publishing the final version allows you to write, be inspired by what you've written, and adapt the earlier parts of the story to fit it before anyone can see it. This is obvious to anyone, but the longer this game goes on and more varying promises get made, it's hard to see everything come together coherently.

It feels like there have already been a ton of threads that have been dropped, and a lot of us are still keeping them in mind to hope they resolve. Things like the machine Maya is in when you meet with HOPE and their angels, the dead rooster in the old half of town, things that just seemed important but have probably been pushed aside.

I hope that it all resolves nicely in the end but it just feels like there are so many things being forgotten at this point that I'll be left wanting

Hey, a silly question, since "Remember to smile" is such a meme, but... do we think it's connected to a particular god/user?

My first thought is HOPE, but...

It first shows up (as near as I can tell) in the Ch.2 scene "The Color White" -- it's one of the many very odd things that Yasu says. Which makes me think it's a HOPE thing (makes sense).

Then the "Smile Reminder" says it a bunch of times during the fourth reset "Ami Bonus Scene," and just after reset 4, Yasu repeats it back to Touka ("Do you remember the advice I gave you, Yasu?") in "Everything, Everywhere, All at Once." So... HOPE again?

Maki says it when you meet up with her right after her husband's death -- sounds like the kind of standard stupid advice people give when someone dies, tbh. But... HOPE? Maybe?

And Kaori (=Sekai=Pareidolia?) says it to Sensei in Sakaki-bar-a (Ch 3, "White Sand Beaches") just after he's had the weird monologue about lamb blood ("And that is why I am still able to smile" -- I'll never look at Passover or Easter the same way again). He's interrupted by an ALL-CAPS NARRATOR -- no initial slashes, so HOPE again, amiright?

HOWEVER...

During the sixth reset, right after Maya Prime's fade-out (Ch 3, "Times New Roman"), the voice on the PA says it when you're first in the escape room. No idea. Might make sense that PA = Wires? But we think the escape room is Pareidolia's, IIRC? Once you get out of the escape room ("Paper City"), you're in a room in "my house" that has REMEMBER TO SMILE repeated on the walls in front of pictures of maggots. (There's forced irony for you!)

The narrator (I think Pareidolia, b/c all lowercase) says it to Sensei in the weird cloud room during the maybe-dream just before the camping trip (Ch 4, "The One with the Happy Ending").

And of course, during the most recent update, the Tree Tickler says it to Sana a couple of times in TSS III. And we've all been thinking Sana's paranormal visitor is Pareidolia, right?

Then there's the smiley face that shows up frequently, including on Tsuneyo's t-shirt -- possibly connected to Wires?

So based on that... it's kind of a phrase that has connections to all of the users/gods? Is it Sel saying, "Don't panic!" just to make us panic?

Or am I missing something? Or overthinking it?

Since aramaug already answered this in a proper manner, I'm gonna jump to the tinfoil: Shiawase Group logo. Remember that HOPE, Wires and Pareidolia are makeshift gods, and Akira has been identified as their "child", although I see that as more of a metaphor. The important thing is that they're fragments of an actual bigger entity, therefore neither of their plans represents the actual original plan.

HOPE wants to purify everything and save only the ascended, Wires wants to create a world where everything bends to Akira's will, Pareidolia wants Akira to accept his inner nature and through that complete the collection, which ultimately leads to a third "better" option. "Remember to Smile" fits neither of these, it seems to be older than them and it's Himawari's message to him at the end of the "Room with the Clocks". All gods have sort of smiling faces as well, so "Remember to Smile" is either the motto of the actual one god, or, and I prefer this take: it's the logo for the foundation behind the simulation.

posts.content_html_raw:
Enezexe said:
Also can someone please tell me the whole story from start? You can give spoilers [...]
Click to expand...
Sure.
Story is about a boy called Akira Arakawa. His mother disliked him and that left a spot open for a predator (his sister-in-law) to enter his home and sexually assault/groom him for years. Eventually that predator became his world, had a child that might have been his, and suddenly died in a horrific accident.

Akira, now an adult, couldn't cope with his abuser being gone for the first time since he was a child, all the while having to care for her/his kid. That led him to establish a sexual relationship with some other runaway child, that was also a survivor of sexual abuse.

Years later, as he lands a teacher position, a mysterious event happens that drags him, his runaway child/girlfriend, and a lot of other people into a time-loop. This time-loop however is not just time-travel, but rather a simulation that is both fake and real at the same time, since even though it's simulated, it's also like a dream being shared by everyone in it = counts as real.

The catch is that everytime a season changes, everyone's memories get modified in an event called a reset, and every few resets, the simulation just hard-resets everyone to their state at the beginning of the first cycle (including Akira's memories). The one person that never loses her memories is his girlfriend, Maya Makinami, that can't tell him about it because it fries his brain everytime she does.

Your journey as a player begins in a cycle like no other, because our Akira (that started and ended as a blank slate in pretty much every other cycle) has started to remember things before the resets, and this cycle gets more unique with every season. You'll soon find out that it's because this cycle is actually a special cycle engineered amidst a battle for control among the divine entities that watch this simulation, with Akira as the their main pawn.

And you'll later find out that this is just a part of a much grander scheme of actual gods watching as these minor/makeshift gods do their thing, but now may also start interfering.
I barely understood anything when I first played the game. I sound like a broken record by now, but it was only after reading the thread and replaying the game that it really clicked for me.

That being said, it's one thing to not understand the supernatural stuff on your first playthrough, it's another for the writing of the events not to get you. If the "harem" part of the plot (girls personal arcs) failed to get your attention, then this is probably not a game for you.

spoilers.html:
Story is about a boy called Akira Arakawa. His mother disliked him and that left a spot open for a predator (his sister-in-law) to enter his home and sexually assault/groom him for years. Eventually that predator became his world, had a child that might have been his, and suddenly died in a horrific accident.

Akira, now an adult, couldn't cope with his abuser being gone for the first time since he was a child, all the while having to care for her/his kid. That led him to establish a sexual relationship with some other runaway child, that was also a survivor of sexual abuse.

Years later, as he lands a teacher position, a mysterious event happens that drags him, his runaway child/girlfriend, and a lot of other people into a time-loop. This time-loop however is not just time-travel, but rather a simulation that is both fake and real at the same time, since even though it's simulated, it's also like a dream being shared by everyone in it = counts as real.

The catch is that everytime a season changes, everyone's memories get modified in an event called a reset, and every few resets, the simulation just hard-resets everyone to their state at the beginning of the first cycle (including Akira's memories). The one person that never loses her memories is his girlfriend, Maya Makinami, that can't tell him about it because it fries his brain everytime she does.

Your journey as a player begins in a cycle like no other, because our Akira (that started and ended as a blank slate in pretty much every other cycle) has started to remember things before the resets, and this cycle gets more unique with every season. You'll soon find out that it's because this cycle is actually a special cycle engineered amidst a battle for control among the divine entities that watch this simulation, with Akira as the their main pawn.

And you'll later find out that this is just a part of a much grander scheme of actual gods watching as these minor/makeshift gods do their thing, but now may also start interfering.

Honestly, I think Himawari has some traits that tend to give her away.

For example: she's not exactly the best at her job:
Sensei - "Wait, how did you know I'm a teacher? I don't remember telling you that."
Himawari - "Uhhhhhhh...hahahah."
(Chapter 3 Maya 'Three Halves Make a Whole (Itadakimasu)' Event) Requires Fingering Ami, and there's a bonus conversation if you're sexing Sara.
Or jobs considering she's been a Scarf Salesperson at the Mall, a Waitress at some French restaurant, and a Melon Salesperson at the New Years Festival.

Sensei has seen through her as Sana as well:
Sensei - "You're not going to question how we've been together for five or six semesters despite still being a first year?"
Himawari-Sana - "Oh! Uhh...has it been that many already? It feels like just yesterday we were meeting one another and-"
Sensei - "Who are you?"
Himawari-Sana - "Oh, God damn it."
(Chapter 3 Sana 'Ad Meliora' Event)
She tends to slip up.

Some other tells/traits that seem to belong to her:
  • Doesn't actually seem to understand things, like the Resets, or what's going on.
  • Has a desire for a designated cafeteria and has coworkers. Also eats Ramen.
  • Has a connection to Sunflowers, Sensei, and Ayane.
  • Has a fondness for Spanish related things. (Like Ayane.)
  • Has a reason (to or) not to reveal certain things, which is implied to affect her future.
  • Has blue eyes. (And probably likes blue considering it seems to be her color of choice)
  • Is a Narrator.
  • Isn't interested in a sexual relationship with Sensei.
  • Is very positive and hopeful.
  • Is working with and seemingly specifically protecting Ayane.
  • Etc
There's probably other things like wanting to see things restored, not being the best at poetry, being jealous of Yumi's boobs, and being scared of Sekai, but those aren't entirely proven to be her, even if they seem likely to be her.

Overall: I think Sel would give at least a notable hint at her being there, instead of another character. It'd be up to the player to decipher it, though.

I'm still curious what was up with the whole offering Sensei some Goat urine to drink, thing, though:
Himawari - "Goat urine?!"
(Chapter 3 'Hiding in Plain Sight' Main Event)
Maybe she was trying to cleanse Sensei from something without being obvious about it?

There's also the whole Ami clone thing, but I don't think that's something we'll understand until we're supposed to.

Amy - "Me too! But, be warned --- it's really easy to get lost in there. So easy that even I get lost sometimes, and I've been here for thousands of years!"
- "Teehee! You should have seen me when I still had hands."
- "Me? I could never. I have a degenerative bone disease and my doctor says extreme sports aren't good for me. But I do know of a shop here that sells them if you want to try!"

Okay, here I go again having to say why having Nozomu be anything more than he already is be a bad idea.
1. Akira's story is that he was disliked by Saki, from which Sekai used that gap to abuse him when he fell from a window at school, by volunteering to take care of him at home. That alone would suggest that Sekai could volunteer to do that, which would put in check her working at the same place as Nozomu.

2. Secondly, Akira choosing to be a teacher is a question of how much he did so by Sekai's influence and how much it was due to try to save people like him. If Nozomu was a teacher, it would simply have to do with following a family tradition, which is never mentioned.

3. Yasu repeatedly states that Saki was more or less responsible for leaving a gap open for Sekai to drag Akira into the darkness, when she says that if she'd been his mother, he would have been loved how he was supposed to be. This suggests that Akira was the one that went wrong, and if Nozomu was the father of half the town, this would make this pointless, as again, it would make it a family tradition rather than something Saki allowed to happen to Akira. It would follow that Akira was expected to turn out just how he did given his brother's inclinations, Sekai or no Sekai.

4. Ami says that Nozomu was a normal dude, and we have confirmation that he was jealous of Akira and Sekai - having him be the father of Shota and Sana would, first, mean not only that he had children even before Sekai got pregnant, but that he was living a very unlikely life if not only for emotional reasons, for time-constraints. And secondly, mean that Ami was wrong about her father (fake), which is not something that Selebus appears to do in his story (when characters reveal something it tends to be the truth).

5. Sekai is a villain of this story, if Nozomu was going around converting everyone to his dick and more or less abusing her too, that not only makes her weaker as a character imo, but it also makes it into a situation where all evil comes from the Arakawa family, which is just ridiculous.

6. There are other minor points, but the most important in my opinion is that while there is merit in making an entire story follow the same overall theme, this does not mean that every evil in the world coming from the same older brother figure that is barely explored is good writing. In fact, it stands in opposition to the actual conflict of the story, which is to which extent it's possible for a groomed kid to seek redemption after having already become a predator himself. It would be extremely lame for Akira to find out after all that that Sekai was pointless, as becoming a predator is "just what's expected of an Arakawa!" [...] The overall theme of this story has not ever been legacy.
As a final note, I don't think it would ruin the story if Nozomu was Sana's father, but it would definitely lessen it by a great deal in my eyes. For him to be involved in more than that would cross even that tenuous line and just make it ridiculous honestly.

Edit: Since so many people are on the fence about this, I reiterate: the only information concerning Nozomu is that he was jealous of Sekai and Akira, that he was a normal person, that he died in the accident alongside Sekai, and that he was Akira's older brother. Being a teacher hasn't ever been alluded to, and, in fact, it's unlikely because both Ami and Akira refer to Sekai when talking about teaching, which would be strange if both of them were - as they'd refer to it as a family thing instead of a Sekai thing. This doesn't mean it's impossible for him to have been one, but it does make it unlikely, as Selebus would be purposefully hiding it from many situations where it would have made sense for it to be aknowledged.

DeanNorris said:
To be fair, "highly likely" was probably a bad choice of wording on my part.
It would make Sana be the most likely connection to Nozomu, out of all the potential bastard daughters. It's not anywhere near confirmed, as you said, there is no real evidence to that at all, but it's hinting towards that from various directions.

During Sana's most recent visit in the TSS shadow LEGENDS™ realm, Pegasus basically makes it clear that he wants to inseminate Sana and hints at having done that to Sara in the past. Or at least that's how I would interpret the following sentence.
View attachment 4020291
So I think it's possible that Sara's teacher was being possessed, or at least influenced, by Pegasus, maybe also HOPE, when he impregnated her. Similar to how Sensei often gets possessed or is being taken over by various entities.
To me, it would be a little random if that happened to just be some unnamed teacher. Instead, it would be somewhat logical if it runs in the family and Nozomu was the one involved. After all the teacher was supposed to be a family man.
Now I'm not as versed with the timeline as the lore masters, but I think it would fit his profile. Besides, Nozomu, the god, is basically either HOPE or connected to HOPE, so it would fit from that perspective as well.

Similarly, it seems a little convenient that Rin does not know anything about her biological parents, except that her Mom was crazy and a slut (if I remember correctly?) and her Dad a scumbag. Yumi's Dad basically raped a passed out druggie. And Chika/Chinami's Dad also was not around.
They all have traits in common, and while it would be absolutely possible for them to be just three different bad dudes, it is awfully vague enough to leave the possibility of there being some higher entity involved that coordinated this.

Again, I might be wrong with a lot of what I'm bringing forth, and I'm not as knowledgeable with the gods and the connections and everything, but I feel like there has been a lot of stuff that hints strongly towards this being a real possibility.

Also, it kind of makes me want to replay the game for the first time finally, to just refresh on a lot of things and make it easier to connect the dots. But I feel like it would take forever at this point.
Click to expand...
There are some things I'd like to add to:
1. Yes, it definitely seems like Pegasus was involved with Sara. But more interestingly, why is Sara regarded as a whore and how did she break free? I think those are the interesting questions. If you'll recall, it wasn't Sara's decision to leave her teacher, it was him that left her. Other than that, it might be that Sara was possessed, not the teacher. As, if you'll also recall, she has experienced blackouts in her past, and yet not anymore. This suggests she was able to cut her connection to the supernatural realm, and their distaste for her henceforth.

2. It's rather expected that Rin doesn't know about her biological parents imo. Why would she? Her mothers know about her biological mother, and it would surprise me if a homossexual couple was that interested in gathering info or wanting to keep in contact with a potential source of trouble for their newly acquired baby. That's not even considering that well, she was trouble (in the medical sense).

3. Yuki's story is complicated. She was not a passed out druggie at that point, she was close to a matron of the Yakuza. She beat Yumi's father entire gang as a teenager (more or less), and went on to live as his girlfriend for years. Mind you, Yumi is considered a princess (considered her father's biological daughter). So it's very unlikely this rape took place at a random alley - rather, it seems likely that it happened at a private gathering of the Yakuza, which would, in turn, make it even more unlikely that Nozomu was also part of the Yakuza to have taken part in this.

4. Chika and Chinami are rather different in age, so he was definitely around enough to have Chinami at least. The same goes for Sana, as Shota was older. What's way more unlikely in my view is that Nozomu went around having Shota, then Chika, then Rin, then Ami (not really), then Sana, then Chinami - and Akira is ten years later retracing his steps unknowingly and because of a different external influence.
Should definitely replay the game though, these are all valid connections to make, I just don't follow them myself.

It was when she was old enough to notice it - and, most importantly, after she was born.
