posts.content_html_raw:
Antosha said:
Hey, I’m sure this has been talked about, but… what is the first divergence Maya noticed from the ever-repeating round of sorrow?

if it was the scarf (which is how I remember it), then Himawari really is a major player, it seems to me. She’s literally changed the unchanging balance in this cycle of misery. She may not be very powerful — she can’t just change stuff. But she’s very important.

And the question of what her role is, not to mention her plan (aside from saving mom and dad) seem pretty central as well.

Not controversial, I know, but interesting.
Click to expand...
Probably Ami becoming a Maid:
Maya Prime - "Are you sure about this?"
Sensei - "Sure about what? Ami getting a job?"
Maya Prime - "It's just not something that's ever happened before."
- "I doubt something this small would have any effect on the world itself, but it's still weird."
(Chapter 1 Ami 'Divergence' Event)
Then the scarf stuff happens.

Although, in theory:
The 'Not Even Me' Chapter 1 Main Event where Sensei runs into Yumi, 3 weeks in, may be the first divergence, and is from the first update.

Maya seemed to think it was odd when Yumi told her about it later in the 'Ponytail' Main Event, then brought this up later to Ami and Sensei in the 'Cursed Birds' Main Event, like it was something new. All before Ami became a Maid and Himawari sold Sensei the scarf in the 'Stray Cat' Chapter 1 Main Event.

What I'm talking about:
Sensei Narrator - "It's been nearly three weeks since I was reborn here."
- "I can see a place where the sidewalk ends- and a glowing passageway of TV static beckoning me forward."
Yumi - "And also, the next time you're out here this late, don't expect me to call out to you again. Got it?"
Sensei Narrator - "It's strange that I ran into her out here so late, but...I'm kind of glad that I did."
- "But because she was able to prevent me from walking toward the light." ("erase yourself" is upside down in the corner, with "i did it again" in the other corner.)
(Chapter 1 'Not Even Me' Main Event)
Yumi - "Like, it was barely a week ago that I caught him wandering the streets at night like some kind of...lost puppy."
Maya Prime - "That's...certainly odd. Even by his standards- which only barely exist from what I've seen thus far."
(Chapter 1 'Ponytail' Main Event)
Maya Prime - "That was a very bad day for me."
- "Have I ever mentioned how intimidating Yumi is?"
(Chapter 1 'Cursed Birds' Main Event)

Of course, there's also how Maya had no idea who Kaori even was, in Chapter 3, and she showed up in Ami's Chapter 1 'The Queen of Spiders' Event. Which was after the Yumi stuff but before the Ami becoming a Maid stuff.

Overall: Ami becoming a Maid is the first notable thing Maya seemed to notice, but it might be Yumi preventing Sensei from seemingly erasing himself/walking into static in 'Not Even Me' that really changed the timeline, if that was new.

Edit: Could be a few other things, though. Hard to tell since Maya focused mostly just on Sensei and Ami.

Gentlemen, I bring you a spoiler from the future.

The Big Joke is that although Sensei appears to be coping with the fact Maya killed herself after he abandoned for fear of becoming a father following a surprise pregnancy, the reality is that Ami killed her and made it look like a suicide. The subsequent interesting part is the way in which Sensei hallucinates Maya as other girls, rather than the other way around. Seeing shards of the same conversations he once held with Maya repeated through the students at various point (hinted at through angling, positions of cats in the background, etc) was the biggest reveal of this update.

"Maya Makinami. Occupation: Student.

She was probably just so used to being insane that it became normal. For example, Himawari couldn't keep up with her mind:
Himawari-Maya - "It's one thing getting inside the head of Yumi or Tsuneyo, but do you have any idea just how much is going on in this one? I can barely make sense of any of it."

(Chapter 3 Maya 'The Sun, And All Its Toxic Rays' Event)
Before giving up.

I think Dean raises a good point, and it's something that I lightly touched upon when I talked about the philosophical implications of someone becoming someone else by losing their memories, to such an extent that it becomes a possible focus of discussion in a plot, but that I don't think Selebus intends to focus on.

DeSkel's explanation seems to be what's intended here: Maya Prime was broken, however that wreck was never meant to be seen by us in its true form, and very likely not even by her. I tend to think that it's either that her mind erased most of her memories naturally (for lack of capacity to hold them)/aided by her being unable to truly break since she's inside kumon-mi; or that she was tampered with by the mechanisms of the resets/makeshift gods (as Tsuneyo implies).

If Maya truly held to all those memories she'd have gone beyond the human condition a long time ago, as people simply cannot retain hundreds of years of memories. Borrowing from both time travel literature, as well as literature that portrays long-lived species such as elves and dragons, an often used explanation is that all those memories are there somewhere, but they get tossed into a sort of archived repository that isn't used in the day-to-day, like a locked partition. I also recall a story in which the immortal had thousands of notebooks about their own life, since they couldn't hold any memory over a thousand years of age (it'd be interesting if that's what's in her box, but no, that's unlikely for a variety of reasons).

On a final note, I'm pretty sure Maya said at one point that she didn't hold that many memories. Like, she remembered overall important points, but everything else became a blur. Which would be a fair explanation for it. But I don't recall when she said this, so it might be my imagination.

In "Rascal doesn't dream of Bunny girl senpai" anime, the MCs little sister loses her memory for two years and becomes a almost complete different person, and when she finally becomes her former self, it has a huge impact on her brother, who got used to her new self.

DeanNorris said:
Now, I will just assume that Sel has not thought it through and my annoyance with this is futile. But there is simply no way that this would be anywhere near possible.
First off, having lived through millions, or even a few thousand, of resets, would make Maya's (mental) age exceed any human being by far. Not only would that have enormous negative effects to one's mental state (and by that I don't mean making Maya "cool and reserved" and somewhat arrogant and all-knowing), it would also make it near impossible for her to reliably remember anything about any previous resets, let alone small details like if Ami ever worked as a maid just once during the previous million timelines.

I just don't understand why Sel chose such a ridiculous amount, and again, if there is any indication that this is meant to be highly exaggerated, please let me know.
Because either, Prime Maya was actually massively mentally fatigued, to the point that she must have been probably hallucinating half of the time, as her capacity for retaining memories would have had to be exceeded at least tenfold. Or, it just felt like she lived through millions of resets, and actually there were only a couple hundred that lasted like 3 days (she did mention that she often just fucked the "bad" Akiras and made them disappear in front of her, I assume making people disappear liek that accelarated the resets? I might remember wrong) and maybe around 50 full on (almost) 1- school-year worth of resets. Which would still make her extremely frustrated and emotionally vacant, but at least to a realistic extent that would be plausible.
Click to expand...
I agree that the supposedly unavoidable effect of repeating timelines on one's mentality seemingly evades Maya, even if some past resets didn't last over 6 months. Regardless, I'd say trying to use her strangely unwavering mental state to question how valid her memory is or the accurate length of the cycled time and would be futile. This part I feel like is intentionally romanticized, portraying Maya as the most unfortunate girl with the undying heart so strong that she would stubbornly wait beyond centuries to hopefully see her loved one again.

One can argue that this alone wouldn't really explain how her mentality survived when she should've gone insane, but I think this is also highly dependent on how the first loop started, how much Maya knew, or even what exactly Maya was even at that given point. So if it's up to me, before the most crucial part of this game is cleared up, for the time being I believe that this is merely a part of her character's side profiling and is effectively exaggeration on Sel's part.

Besides, there is no real or possible investigation on how many years worth of memories one can hold without going insane. The best argument anyone can bring up is "Oh I watched an anime about this once that talked about this subject in depth so it is definitely a better source material than whatever light novel your read". To me that's just people throwing questionable arguments at each other when instead it all comes down the dev's creative license and nothing more.

As for how valid her memories are with this emerging mental issue, I think the fact that all past resets being extremely repetitive helps her spot bigger anomalies that never appeared before, and Ami working as a maid isn't a small change at all (in fact it was prompted by Sensei so arguably this might be a ripple of real Sensei returning to his body).

That sounds like her last words before she got reset, so it makes sense. Other than that, iirc it has always been a mixture of Maya avoiding time-based questions and white lying to Sensei to conceal information if she ever said something in the past being a blur to her.

Both those titles are pretty exciting. USER4 hype for the first one? And the second one has a bunch of connections:

The phrases "a house near a lake" and "the same place as always" appear together in a twitter poem from Miu. In addition to "same place as always", the poem's line "in the event you overslept" is a direct quotation of the mystery MM note.

I don't see how/why Miu would be leaving notes for Akira, so this seems more likely to be a case of patterns repeating themselves, but who knows.

There are clues in the house near the lake according to Tsuneyo/Wires.
This is probably the same as Ami's grandma's house, especially given it's importance from before Akira was born.
I presume this is Saki's house, which would connect back to Miu's poem and NiB. It doesn't make sense for it to be Akira's childhood home next to the Nakayamas, though, so I'm not sure how that fits in. Maybe Saki lived in the lake house when she was younger, it stayed in the family, and at some point she moved back and left her kids in the city?

The phrase "same place as always" also applies to the roof during the resets. That's the assumed meaning in the MM note, and Maya has used a similar phrase.
The phrase is also explicitly used for the roof in a message that Yasu receives during the Chapter 2 beach trip, possibly from Maya Prime.

So I'm not sure which direction this event is going to go in, but in any case we should get some good lore clues out of it. I'm hopeful, but not very expectant, that Maya Prime will be involved given her connection with "same place as always" and Nao's involvement in the TSS.

posts.content_html_raw:
LoveBlueHairedGirl said:
So, want to have a distraction? As a ficwriter (I will never show my actual fanfiction here) here are some random ideas:

Imagine Chinami as a mature woman with her own daughter which she called after her late mother. It would be wholesome, isn't it? The father might or not might be Sensei.

Imagine Io without the things what happened with her at 5... How will it change her? Will she still love the craft?

Imagine if there was a real police force in this universe. How quickly would Akira end up in jail?

Or what if there no cycles at all.
Click to expand...
Honestly some pretty cool concepts here. I’m also a writer, and often like to envision potential ‘what-if’ scenarios in franchises I like. It’s honestly one of my favorite pastimes.

If someone were to try and make a short story out of this, I’d read and critique it. I already RP on Discord anyway with LiL characters in the form of a story, so hey. I’m used to it.
LoveBlueHairedGirl said:
Also there are some questions for you guys:

Imagine yourself in a past, studying in a class with main cast. Who will you be friends with, who will you argue with? Do not think of some meta information or gods stuff. Think about girls' personalities and how they act.
Click to expand...
Not taking into account meta or game knowledge and just the characters themselves? I’d get along really well with Chika, Uta, Futaba, Noriko and Rin. Those five seem very sociable and like they can get along with pretty much anyone who’s decent. Molly and Miku also seem friendly, so perhaps they’d also be potential candidates.

As for who I wouldn’t get along with? Definitely Yumi, despite how much I like her as a character and would like to say differently. At first, there’s no shot she wouldn’t be standoffish towards me, and with no knowledge of her in-game, I’d just assume she was a bitch and that was it. Maya and I also wouldn’t get along on account of how reserved she is and how she sticks to her own small circle of friends. I probably wouldn’t bother.
LoveBlueHairedGirl said:
Also, imagine yourself part of some family in LiL. Which family you would prefer to be born into? Like, tell me if you prefer to be someone's son or brother. Or even a daugher/sister.
Click to expand...
Instinct tells me to immediately latch onto the Tsukioka family to be born into. You’ll be rich and set for life. But the more you think about it, the more you realize just how sheltered you’d be from the outside world until a certain age where you’ll be forced to adapt. And even then, that can prove very challenging unless you’re thrown straight into the fire. Assuming you weren’t, the process would take even longer to overcome. Besides, Touka and Tsukasa’s parents aren’t… the best, putting it lightly.

With that in mind, I might choose to be born a Nakayama. I get to have a rich, idol sister, so money still isn’t a concern. And at the same time, I have two (incredibly hot) sisters who I know I can rely on. Not to mention the game has given no indication that their parents are bad in any way. It seems like a solid family all around.
LoveBlueHairedGirl said:
And which one of the girls you'll want to be real? As part of your family? Or as some random girl you suddenly meet with?
Click to expand...
Y’know, unironically, I’d love to have Ami as a family member. She might be a liiiiittle fucking insane sometimes, but at least she’s loyal. Plus, she makes breakfast! Come on!
LoveBlueHairedGirl said:
Anyway, here is the sad part about irl stuff.
The doctor thinks I might have cancer. So I recently took tests and now I am waiting for the results to come back and I will also be going to see an oncologist in the coming days. If the cancer is confirmed, I don't even know if I will be able to live to the end of LiL. Though considering I am still okay for now, I would be okay. Right?
Click to expand...
Holy fuck, dude… I’m really sorry to hear about that, and for what it’s worth, I’ll be keeping you in my thoughts. Hopefully the results will come back as a false alarm, but in the event that the worst becomes true, I have this to say:

Kick that cancer’s ass. You can do it! The good part is that now you’re aware of it. The best way to handle things from here is figuring out the extent of your results and seeing what can be done.

I’m confident you’ll be right here posting with us when the ending to Lessons in Love comes out years from now. It’s something to look forward to.

Anyway, again, best of luck to you! You got this.

Imagine yourself in a past, studying in a class with main cast. Who will you be friends with, who will you argue with? Do not think of some meta information or gods stuff. Think about girls' personalities and how they act.

Also, imagine yourself part of some family in LiL. Which family you would prefer to be born into? Like, tell me if you prefer to be someone's son or brother. Or even a daugher/sister.

And which one of the girls you'll want to be real? As part of your family? Or as some random girl you suddenly meet with?

LoveBlueHairedGirl said:
So, want to have a distraction? As a ficwriter (I will never show my actual fanfiction here) here are some random ideas:

Imagine Chinami as a mature woman with her own daughter which she called after her late mother. It would be wholesome, isn't it? The father might or not might be Sensei.

Imagine Io without the things what happened with her at 5... How will it change her? Will she still love the craft?

Imagine if there was a real police force in this universe. How quickly would Akira end up in jail?

Or what if there no cycles at all.

Also there are some questions for you guys:

Imagine yourself in a past, studying in a class with main cast. Who will you be friends with, who will you argue with? Do not think of some meta information or gods stuff. Think about girls' personalities and how they act.

Also, imagine yourself part of some family in LiL. Which family you would prefer to be born into? Like, tell me if you prefer to be someone's son or brother. Or even a daugher/sister.

And which one of the girls you'll want to be real? As part of your family? Or as some random girl you suddenly meet with?

Anyway, here is the sad part about irl stuff.
The doctor thinks I might have cancer. So I recently took tests and now I am waiting for the results to come back and I will also be going to see an oncologist in the coming days. If the cancer is confirmed, I don't even know if I will be able to live to the end of LiL. Though considering I am still okay for now, I would be okay. Right?
Click to expand...
Sad part:
No matter what, I wish you the best.

The ideas:
Chinami: Honestly, it depends on if Chinami's condition is inherited by her children like it seemed to be from her mother. Not to mention, Sensei's psychosis on top of that would make me pity the fuck out of those kids.

In a happily ever after way though, I'd like to think Chinami becomes a part of the Tsukioka Family and they help her and her kids get all the help possible and they all live a fulfilling life with as many pools of jello as they want.

Io: Completely different person I'd wager, but that depends on who raises her. Without her trauma, she'd also probably never meet Uta or have such a disdain for women.

Police: Depends on those around Sensei, tbh. The likes of Noriko, Niki, Ami, Maya, etc would probably never turn him in, and the likes of Niki and Ayane would probably pay off whoever, however they could. Still waiting to see how Ayane handles the pedo stuff, though, especially since her whole thing is wanting to be a mother...I struggle to see how any worthwhile mother would just overlook the idea of someone molesting their wizard...or someone else's. Same with any worthwhile father.

No Cycles: Depends on what started them and why. Although, presumably, Sensei would just be with Maya and basically Sensei, Ami, and Maya would be happy, and Ayane would be happy-ish, unless she was serious about blowing up the city if Sensei never accepts her by the end of Highschool.

Rin and Chika might be together, and since they both work and have a lot of love and lust, they'd probably be doing rather well. Chinami would have another big sister, and I can see Rika and Chinami getting along. Rika might make a decent babysitter, assuming she screws up things with Rin's other mom still.

Futaba is like a sister to Rin, so Chinami probably ends up with a few more sisters in this timeline. (Nodoka then corrupts Chinami once she hits puberty)

Yumi and Rin would probably clash over Futaba, though, and well, Chika never liked that part of Yumi either. So, optimistically, Yumi straightens up before it affects Rin's and Chika's relationship. Not sure if Yuki or Kaori ever come up.

Most others probably just end up where they were heading.

Imagine:
Friends: Strangely enough, maybe Yumi. Only because I can relate to her far more than I'd like to, and I'm anti-drugs as well. I feel like we'd have an understanding, at least. I'd also say Futaba, since she's well, Futaba. Although, I have a feeling that me and Kirin would be hanging out a lot, and I'm not entirely proud of why. I could also see me and Yasu, Tsuneyo, and Io, getting along.

It really just depends on who I'd want to be friends with at the time, and who I wouldn't, and if I'm in the mood for drama.

Family: Amamiyas. Being Rich sounds nice, and there's more freedom there than with the Tsukiokas. Having neglectful parents isn't anything new, and having Ayane as a sister wouldn't be that bad.

Real: Karin? Like, in any way, a Karin would always be welcome.

Nobodyknowsmeok said:
Is this game the best there is? I just started playing these type of games and I feel like I won't find one as good as this lol
Click to expand...
Currently yes, but whereas the quality of the "harem plot" can be observed without an ending, the same cannot be said for the overall plot and especially how derivative/verbose the supernatural elements are. We're hoping for the best on that front.
Also, you can find a lot of adult games with a compelling story, it really is limited usually by the gameplay. A lot of them are in rpgm for instance, and others are in some sort of unity-esque stuff that wastes about hours of your time just trying to find a way to change the code to get over the annoying and unnecessary parts of the gameplay that stand between you and the plot.

Sierra Lee's work has been recognized multiple times, especially with The Last Sovereign, which is free on steam. Noblesse Oblige is a game that is clearly inspired by it, and it is overall interesting but rather early in its development (it takes you about two days to finish, it's just that the scope is massive). I just finished playing How to Build a Magnificent Kingdom, and was very pleasantly surprised by some elements of the plot.

I mention this last one specifically because, as is the case for many passion projects, you'll usually find a very interesting part of the story and will have to ignore a lot of the others. For Renpy games, the landscape is rather atrocious story-wise, even the good tends to look ridiculous when compared to LiL.
Edit: Just an off-topic mention, but recently I bought the Class of '09 on steam, and some aspects of its synopsis reminded me of DeSkel's Dark Route. Basically you're a senior girl in highschool that has to be mean to all these people that either want something from you or just to fuck you, cause if you don't you'll end up in truly horrifying scenarios. I think Ami would like it.

Just going to point out to you guys that this douche is an edgelord troll, by replying to him all you're doing is feeding his need for attention and he will continue to make bullshit pseudo-intellectual arguments to justify his stance just so you'll try and counter-argue whatever shit he spews, it's a waste of time and he gets off on it so just ignore him.
Click to expand...
yep, another one to the ignore list.
Vizer007 said:
To be fair, the only qualms I have with recommending SO is that it's not finished and never will. There are so many popular work made by deranged and fkd up people the bad deeds of which were either never found or just kept under rugs. People just don't know. The only thing that matters is that the work is good to enjoy and the animal is behind bars. There is no need to ruin the good time for people who is not in the know.
Click to expand...
I half-agree with this. I am of the camp that the work is separate from the artist, however, that should be up to the reader. Wouldn't reading a book about serial killers written by a serial killer potentially sweeten the pot for some people?
I think that people that want to consume a piece of work that involves some level of fictional pedophilia should be also assumed to be adult enough to not have it "ruined" to them by someone stating facts about the author of said work. Ultimately, it is up to the reader to find that a dealbreaker or not.

Regardless, sensei overnight is a mess of a game. As is lost in you, but less so. Superhuman was very interesting in the beginning and then it really derailed for me, becoming less of an occult and bizarre game to an academy of superheroes linear plot. I think no one has suggested this, but sometimes it's good to go back to the classics too. Playing Tsukihime, Higurashi, even Fate to a lesser extent, would not be a waste of time (vn wise). Steins;Gate would also be interesting, but more for an overall time-travel game.

Also, outside of the games, anyone that enjoys LiL (the harem part especially) should really watch the entirety of the Monogatari Series. It is a masterpiece of writing and the way the story is structured is akin to a sort of "piece it together yourself" overall narrative that is also one of the most defining aspects of LiL. There are a bunch of different ways to watch the series, but basically just start with Bakemonogatari. If someone ever wants me to, I can talk at length about the series.

Keep the faith and may everything favor you, including possibly being nothing.

A lot of them are in rpgm for instance, and others are in some sort of unity-esque stuff that wastes about hours of your time just trying to find a way to change the code to get over the annoying and unnecessary parts of the gameplay that stand between you and the plot.

Sierra Lee's work has been recognized multiple times, especially with The Last Sovereign, which is free on steam. Noblesse Oblige is a game that is clearly inspired by it, and it is overall interesting but rather early in its development (it takes you about two days to finish, it's just that the scope is massive). I just finished playing How to Build a Magnificent Kingdom, and was very pleasantly surprised by some elements of the plot.

I mention this last one specifically because, as is the case for many passion projects, you'll usually find a very interesting part of the story and will have to ignore a lot of the others. For Renpy games, the landscape is rather atrocious story-wise, even the good tends to look ridiculous when compared to LiL.

spoilers.title: further thoughs and recommendations
spoilers.html:
I think that people that want to consume a piece of work that involves some level of fictional pedophilia should be also assumed to be adult enough to not have it "ruined" to them by someone stating facts about the author of said work. Ultimately, it is up to the reader to find that a dealbreaker or not.

Regardless, sensei overnight is a mess of a game. As is lost in you, but less so. Superhuman was very interesting in the beginning and then it really derailed for me, becoming less of an occult and bizarre game to an academy of superheroes linear plot. I think no one has suggested this, but sometimes it's good to go back to the classics too. Playing Tsukihime, Higurashi, even Fate to a lesser extent, would not be a waste of time (vn wise). Steins;Gate would also be interesting, but more for an overall time-travel game.

Also, outside of the games, anyone that enjoys LiL (the harem part especially) should really watch the entirety of the Monogatari Series. It is a masterpiece of writing and the way the story is structured is akin to a sort of "piece it together yourself" overall narrative that is also one of the most defining aspects of LiL. There are a bunch of different ways to watch the series, but basically just start with Bakemonogatari. If someone ever wants me to, I can talk at length about the series.

I've always wanted to ask, do we know what these really are about? Or better yet, do we know who exactly is behind that Himawari account along with those wiki edits? I am in the process of deciding how serious I want to look at these.

My strongest reason is that, like any other documented item, information should flow to wiki and get summarized there (and get agreed upon many as one extra QA step), and not the other way around where you can find information on the wiki that looks seemingly important but literally doesn't exist anywhere in the source materials.

I'd give passes to miscellaneous, trivial, and unimportant character facts like blood types. I can tolerate these information being mentioned only in wiki and never elsewhere, but not when the information has enough impact or is tied to the most mysterious figures in the game. Where did you learn this from even? If I can decide, the chance of Selly himself or someone endorsed by him doing these edits is so microscopic compared to the chance of a group of nitwits doing heavy RP and pulling everyone's leg.

Despite me saying that, I noticed I've given one pass to the Are You Happy Here Twitter account along with all the mumble jumble there, but only because that account just looks like a dev shitposting epicenter in which everything there is elusive as fuck anyway; it is not equivalent to finding stuff on the wiki that you can't even reference.

(Concerning seasons and resets) Just a "the more you know" moment, cause the more active members of the thread will know this, but I'd wager many people don't:

A reset should equate to the changing of the four seasons. Therefore a cycle is, in essence, Summer (Hope) -> Fall (USER4) -> Winter (Wires) -> Spring (Pareidolia). Hence, a reset happens on either an equinox or a solstice. This is important to grasp because, when LiL starts, Fall and Spring have been taken - but not their slots.

That's why you get Summer -> Fall Summer -> Winter -> Spring Winter -> Summer -> Fall Summer -> Winter Spring. As you can see, seasons have lasted two resets up until this point because they were occupying the missing season slots.

This has not been confirmed in game, but I feel pretty safe in assuming this is the way it is. Furthermore, Spring can include a reset without changing to another season, in actual fact, the following season would be Spring's original slot (the current should have been Winter).

This is not a theory I'm invested in, but I'll try to help with another's theorycrafting.
A way to look at this is that the Original Akira was responsible for the cycles (most likely alongside Maya). So we have Akira and Maya at the room of the clocks, because they both are resetting the world (mostly Akira) everytime he doesn't get to the worldstate he wants.

Since gods seem to be real, and have offices and stuff, it's possible that Maya and Original Akira entered into a covenant with actual deities to make all of this possible, likely with deities that were already involved with the events of the previous game, thus explaining why "it all started before you were born, on a house by the lake". Hence, the gate had already been tampered with, Akira and Maya just renewed the contract, or made a new one, idk.

Well, Akira failed. He failed so many times that he broke, and Maya couldn't convince him to stop turning back the clocks. So their perfect simulation also began to break down. No longer they had four seasons, no longer they had a whole Akira, his mind split and out of it came makeshift beings to keep control over the simulation. These are the makeshift gods: HOPE, Wires, Pareidolia, and USER4. Each of them responsible for 1/4 of the simulation.

For some reason, Pareidolia and USER4 were unable to keep control of it though, leaving it all to HOPE and Wires for the longest time. As for Akira, since he was split, there was no more actual Akira, only fragments of him, that the makeshift gods threw time and time again into the cycles. So, really, it's just big fragments of Akira toying with smaller fragments of Akira, all trying to fullfill a directive from when he was one whole thing instead of this mess.

Therefore, a glowing ball of light, a tree with roots of wire, a voice inside your head, and an unconscious formless force, when eventually put together, should bring back the original Akira that started the simulation.
Or, you know, not. I don't really take after this one.

posts.content_html_raw: You have now read around four hundred events in Lessons in Love (the game) and you're becoming caught up in the story. At a certain point you remark: "This sentence sounds somehow familiar. In fact, this whole passage reads like something I've read before." Of course: there are themes that recur, the text is interwoven with these reprises, which serve to express the fluctuation of time. You are the sort of reader who is sensitive to such refinements; you are quick to catch the author's intentions and nothing escapes you. But, at the same time, you also feel a certain dismay; just when you were beginning to grow truly interested, at this very point the author feels called upon to display one of those virtuoso tricks so customary in modern writing, repeating a paragraph word for word. Did you say paragraph? Why, it's a whole event; you make the comparison, he hasn't changed even a comma. And as you continue, what develops? Nothing: the narration is repeated, identical to the events you have read! You have flown into a web of post-modern metafiction wherein things reset then restart.

You have now read around four hundred events in Lessons in Love (the game) and you're becoming caught up in the story. At a certain point you remark: "This sentence sounds somehow familiar. In fact, this whole passage reads like something I've read before." Of course: there are themes that recur, the text is interwoven with these reprises, which serve to express the fluctuation of time. You are the sort of reader who is sensitive to such refinements; you are quick to catch the author's intentions and nothing escapes you. But, at the same time, you also feel a certain dismay; just when you were beginning to grow truly interested, at this very point the author feels called upon to display one of those virtuoso tricks so customary in modern writing, repeating a paragraph word for word. Did you say paragraph? Why, it's a whole event; you make the comparison, he hasn't changed even a comma. And as you continue, what develops? Nothing: the narration is repeated, identical to the events you have read! You have flown into a web of post-modern metafiction wherein things reset then restart.

good effort, but I'm the resident specialist of quotting random obscure stuff into a wall of text:
Do you remember the first time we touched hands? It happened by accident on the floor of your bedroom. At first I thought there was no way you'd ever see me in that light. But when all the other lights burned out, and I was still there, I finally understood: You were just as broken as me. And I knew then and there that I would fall unto you.

Do you remember the first time you told me you loved me? It was snowing. I confessed my feelings to you weeks prior and you had been sitting on your decision ever since. When you uttered those words, it was like my heart stopped. Like everything I've ever wanted was finally mine. And I could finally be happy. You took me to your room and took my panties off. You put your fingers inside me and I started crying. But they were happy tears - because I finally knew what it meant to be loved.

Forget everything you know about love. Forget everything you know about her. Give unto me what you're incapable of giving to anyone else. Only then can you be saved. I'm doing this for your own good.

We are all just air, so take a deep breath, and get ready to jump once more. One more clock on the wall. Nothing falls but me. Everything falls but me. This a test of the emergency broadcast system. There is no need to panic. Any interruptions you might experience, included but not limited to: visual disturbances, heightened senses of spirituality, or the changing of seasons, can simply be ignored. Everything is fine. Please continue to look up.

The coarseness of the ground upon which you sit tears microscope holes in the fabric of a young girl's dress. It captivates you, like an unobscured horizon, or a beautiful bird you are seeing for the first time; A heron comes to mind. You find yourself pondering the difference light can make and why some things are so much prettier when left unlit. You forget this. Your mind goes somewhere else. You follow it. You end up in front of a well. You look down. But when your eyes make contact with the bottom, you realize that it is you that you are looking down upon. When you blink, you are back at home. Safe and sound. Perhaps it is time to start wearing denim.

You cannot choose. You have already made your choice. Throw your heart into the wishing well. Here, only pain exists. This town has two halves. Please, remember to smile.

We've got you! HimawariCo. is dedicated to preventing unintentional information from clogging up your mind. It's okay! Wherever you are, you can count on us! Really! You can! Satisfaction guaranteed! For real!

At the end of every hallway. Until the end of time, Friend. And even beyond it. Take this gift from those that think you need it. Pareidolia will have my head for this, but I know from experience that wires can only do so much. Wrong turn? Do not listen to the voices, they want to confuse you. Look for my signs, they're dressed in blue. You cannot hear us, but we are coming for you. Over these unventured hills we climb. With canisters of light.
Edit: Please continue to enjoy Lessons in Love in its purest form as you grow closer to Akira Arakawa and his many companions.
Edit2: I also wonder if someone managed to identify from whence all the quotes come from.
